title: The Ledger of Valparaíso
premise: In 1891 Valparaíso, on the eve of Chile's civil war, Sebastian Brightwater — a woman passing as her late father's apprentice in his typeface-cutting shop — is left an infant at the door by a fleeing naval officer, along with a forged baptismal ledger page and one instruction: forget my face. The child, she discovers, is the illegitimate daughter of a congressman now declared an enemy of the Balmaceda government, and the ledger page is proof that could save or hang him. As bombardment closes over the harbor and government agents search print shops for seditious type, Sebastian must choose between the loyalty she owes her dead father's trade and patrons, and the truth pressed into her hands in ink still wet. She keeps her promise by printing the truth herself, at terrible cost, and ends the war having lost the shop but gained a family she chose.
about_author: Oscar Thackeray is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in port cities from Callao to Cardiff. The Ledger of Valparaíso grew out of a salvaged Chilean jobbing press and the unanswered questions of everyone whose names never made it into official histories.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink and Salt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet the Brightwater print shop above the harbor: her father's death, her disguise as his male apprentice 'Sebastián,' and the fragile routine that keeps her secret safe. Emotional beat: guarded contentment built on concealment, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. During a storm, a naval officer leaves an infant, a folded ledger page, and coins, whispering 'forget my face' before vanishing into the fog. She takes the child in against every instinct for survival. Beat: fear cracking open into reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Baptismal Page
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Examining the forged ledger entry, she recognizes her father's own cutting style in the type — someone used their shop years ago to falsify a birth record. The child has a name: Almendra. Beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Don Fermín's Request
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Congressman Fermín Undurraga, a longtime patron, commissions pamphlets defending the opposition — and mentions, obliquely, a daughter he believes dead. Sebastian realizes the baby is his. Beat: the weight of knowledge she cannot share.

chapters.title: Sergeant Roldán Calls
chapters.summary: Roldán's POV. A government agent inspects the shop for seditious type, courteous and menacing. He notices small things — the size of the apprentice's hands, the fresh milk. Beat: the noose tightening while smiles remain fixed.

chapters.title: What Peacetime Promised
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback woven through present. Years earlier, Fermín saved her father from debtors' prison; her father swore a debt of honor. Now she understands the promise made in peacetime now binds her to a man declared enemy. Beat: duty revealed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Wet Nurse of Cerro Alegre
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She smuggles Almendra up the hill to Doña Peta, a widowed laundress, inventing a story about a drowned sister. First bombardment rumors reach the city. Beat: love expressed as logistics, terror beneath competence.

chapters.title: Type Stolen in the Night
chapters.summary: Apprentice-mate Tomás's POV. Someone breaks in and steals matrices bearing the shop's distinctive private typefaces — the very ones that could prove the forgery. Suspicion falls inward. Beat: betrayal inside the walls.

chapters.title: Congress Flees, the Fleet Turns
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. News breaks: Congress has fled aboard the warships; civil war is declared. Fermín is officially a traitor. Harbor life fractures between loyalists and rebels. Beat: the world she knew dissolving overnight.

chapters.title: Forget My Face
chapters.summary: Naval officer Iriarte's POV, interwoven with Sebastian finding his trail. The officer who left the baby is dying of wounds aboard a rebel ship; he sent word asking whether the child lives. Beat: guilt and hope traveling by smuggled note.

chapters.title: Roldán's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Roldán's POV. He returns with the stolen matrices recovered from a fence — and a proposition: identify Fermín's collaborators or the shop burns as a rebel press. He lets slip he knows 'Sebastián' is a woman. Beat: blackmail wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: The Debt Called In
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Fermín, hiding in the city disguised as a dockworker, comes to her at night. He asks not for shelter but for the ledger page — proof his daughter lived, and evidence that could clear him of treason charges built on the forged record. Beat: promise and peril finally the same object.

chapters.title: Tomás's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Revealed as Roldán's informant, motivated by family held hostage, Tomás wrestles with what he's done. He warns Sebastian without confessing fully. Beat: loyalty vs. truth embodied in one compromised man.

chapters.title: Bombardment Begins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The fleet shells the harbor forts; the city empties toward the hills. The shop's windows shatter; the press survives under sandbags. Sebastian retrieves Almendra amid chaos. Beat: war arriving not as politics but as noise and dust.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Studying the ledger page, she proves her father cut the original matrices under coercion years ago — meaning the Brightwaters are already entangled in Fermín's enemies' plot. Her family name is on the crime. Beat: memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: What the Press Can Say
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She resolves to print the true story — the forged record, the living heir, the frame-up — using the surviving type, knowing it will destroy the shop and expose her identity. Beat: quiet resolve, love against duty resolved in favor of truth.

chapters.title: The Night Composition
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás returns, confesses all, and sets type beside her through the night — redemption in lead and ink. They print two hundred copies of 'The Ledger.' Beat: forgiveness earned by shared labor.

chapters.title: Roldán Comes at Dawn
chapters.summary: Roldán's POV then Sebastian's. Roldán arrives to arrest them as the first copies leave via laundry carts. Confrontation in the wrecked shop; Tomás shields them; Roldán hesitates when shown the proof implicating his own superiors. Beat: climax of loyalties.

chapters.title: Fire on Quebrada Street
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Government loyalists torch the shop; Sebastian saves only the ledger, the infant, and one salvaged matrix — her father's first-cut letter, an S. Iriarte, ashore and dying, sees Almendra alive and dies at peace. Beat: loss and release entwined.

chapters.title: The Fall of the President
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Balmaceda's defeat at Placilla; the pamphlets circulate through the victorious army; Fermín is cleared and restored. Roldán, having switched sides quietly, loses interest in Sebastian — or chooses to forget her face. Beat: history turning, indifferent to individuals.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Ruin
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Among the ashes, Fermín offers to legitimize Almendra and asks Sebastian to stay as his house's printer — but she must decide whether to keep living as Sebastián. She claims her own name aloud for the first time. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Setting New Type
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, a rebuilt small press near Doña Peta's laundry prints wedding invitations, broadsheets, and a children's alphabet — each S cut by hand. Almendra sleeps in a drawer of type cases. Beat: memory honored, future composed letter by letter.
